sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (23 August 2012, as amended)
Luxembourg-United States Tax Convention (24 May 2000, as amended)
Luxembourg-China Double Taxation Agreement (17 March 1983, as amended by Protocol of 29 March 2020)
Luxembourg-France Double Taxation Agreement (1 April 1993, as amended)
BLEU-India Bilateral Investment Treaty (1998, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (CSSF AML Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) implementing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law of 1 December 1978 on administrative procedure; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 February 2020 on UBO disclosure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Excerpt from Foreign Trade Register for each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate UBO or shareholder if available
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent notarial authority of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy of each director, managing officer, shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary / Ministry of Foreign Affairs of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each UBO, manager and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank or competent local authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and professional relationship for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution of the UBO's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and controlling officers against European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, United States OFAC specially designated nationals (SDN) list, and the Luxembourg national sanctions and restrictive measures list under the CSSF AML regime. PEP status must be assessed using EU AMLD4/AMLD5 definitions; Politically Exposed Persons, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification and senior management approval before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via Luxembourg Business Registers - www.lbrc.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Luxembourg company names must be in Latin script; the primary legal language for registration is French, while German and Luxembourgish are accepted. Non-Latin names are not registrable unless accompanied by a statutorily valid transliteration into Latin characters. The legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or abbreviation 'SARL' must be included exactly.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name search and non-confirmation certificate must be obtained through an approved notary or the RCS portal. RCS name clearance remains valid for 30 calendar days. If rejected, submit an online administrative re-examination request through MyGuichet within 5 business days; if the re-examination is denied, appeal by way of a motion for annulment (recours en annulation) before the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within 3 months of notification under the Law of 1 December 1978 on administrative procedure. Notarial assistance is required for any extension and for the final adoption of the articles of association.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed domiciliation agent registered with the Luxembourg business register and subject to CSSF oversight. A pure virtual office or mail-only address is not permissible as the sole registered office of a Luxembourg SARL. The registered office must be physically located in Luxembourg and constituted as the entity's administrative seat, even for e-commerce print-on-demand retail activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% (Low-Medium risk); probability increases if a domiciliation agent without physical heritage is used, if management is non-Luxembourg resident, or if substance indicators are absent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name search, availability certificate and preliminary due diligence extraction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for electronic register consultation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign corporate and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Consular posts / apostille authority of origin country
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document apostille fee plus handling service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial preparation and execution of Luxembourg SARL articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under Luxembourg Law of 27 March 1979

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing and electronic publication of deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers and Recueil électronique des sociétés (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: RCS filing fee and RESA publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation agreement (12-month prepaid commitment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk e-commerce retail SARL

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC compliance package, PEP and sanctions screening of UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance review fee per corporate structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register (RBE) initial declaration preparation and filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RBE registrar via the national reporting platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for notary or authorized agent preparation; RBE filing itself is without tax or fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, typically EUR 280-450 per hour plus fixed drafting fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Articles 180-206 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée, SARL); supplemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and the electronic gazette (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) filed with the RCS and published in the electronic gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations – RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 for an SARL, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash or in kind at incorporation. The capital must be deposited into a blocked bank account opened in the name of the company 'in formation' and released only upon RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital of the Company of EUR 12,000 be allotted to the incorporators, all shares being fully paid in cash. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [Registered Address, L-1111 Luxembourg], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that the incorporators approve the first call on shares and that the subscription amounts be held in the Company's capital account. RESOLVED, that [Full Name] be appointed as sole Manager (Gérant) and [Full Name] as Deputy Manager, each with authority to act singly on behalf of the Company. RESOLVED, that all actions taken to effect the incorporation and to open bank accounts are hereby ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Negative Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS database for the proposed company name; if available, apply online for a 'certificat de non-confusion' (negative certificate). The certificate confirms that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Submit the certificate to the notary for the deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (three alternatives recommended)
Founder identification documents (passport or national ID)
Proof of address of each founder
Draft articles of incorporation (Article of Purpose in French or German preferred)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, file a new request with alternative names; if approved but later contested at notarization, undertake a formal opposition procedure before the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) or Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked deposit account designated in the name of 'SARL [Name] in formation' with a Luxembourg bank or before the notary. Deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 12,000 in cash (or effect in-kind contributions with a statutory auditor's report). Obtain from the bank the attestation of capital blocking and the certificate of deposit, which will be presented to the notary.
required_dossiers: Draft notarial deed of incorporation
Negative certificate issued by the RCS
Passport/ID and proof of address of each founder
Client acceptance forms and economic beneficial owner declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or refuses, select another Luxembourg credit institution or request the notary to act as depositary; (for in-kind contributions) if the auditor's report fails, adjust the valuation and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear personally or through a duly constituted attorney before the Luxembourg notary, who then solemnly verifies legal capacity, capital deposit, and the legality of the articles. The notary formally reads and signs the deed of incorporation, thereby incurring the legal existence of the SARL as of the date of signature; the notary also prepares the file for RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Negative certificate
Blocked capital attestation (bank or notary deposit certificate)
Draft articles of incorporation
Passport/ID and proof of address of founders and designated managers
Certificate of non-conviction (for managers, if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a query, amend the articles (e.g., clarify the corporate object or capital provisions) and attend a new appointment; if a founder fails to appear, execute by power of attorney.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Trade and Companies Register and Publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the original deed and all supporting documents with the RCS. Upon review, the RCS assigns the company's national identification number (matricule), formally registers the company, and publishes the incorporation in the electronic gazette (RESA). The company acquires full legal personality as of the RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Original notarial deed of incorporation
Blocked capital attestation
Negative certificate
Written consent of the registered office owner or lease agreement
Proof of address of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the file, correct the identified formalities (usually within 10 working days) and resubmit via the notary; if the objection concerns the corporate purpose, amend the articles by notarial supplementary deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of the First Board Meeting and Adoption of Governance Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators convene the inaugural management meeting to formally allot the issued shares, confirm the registered office address, appoint the Manager (Gérant) and any Deputy Manager, approve the pro-forma board resolution, and open the statutory registers. The decision is recorded in the minutes, signed by the Manager(s), and filed in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Share subscription list
Pro-forma first board resolution
Express acceptance and signature of the appointed Manager(s)
Utility bill or lease agreement for the registered office
Opening bank account documentation (if additional to the blocked capital account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a dispute arises over appointments, call an extraordinary general meeting and resolve by written resolution per the articles; if the prior registered office consent is withdrawn, promptly execute a change of registered office and notify the RCS.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale du commerce et de l'artisanat (Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Commerce and Crafts)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory operating license is required for the SARL's pure e-commerce print-on-demand retail activity (ISIC 4791); the business is statutorily exempt from a municipal commercial establishment license under the laws applicable to distance selling.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No mandatory EIA: the activity is classified as Category 5 (Annex IV of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental assessment), comprising non-industrial online retail; however, general environmental duties under the Law of 21 June 1976 apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For online retail and POD printing at a non-industrial scale, applicable standards include municipal wastewater discharge limits, VOC emissions within threshold values under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 August 2023, and adherence to Directive 2008/98/EC for waste handling and disposal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No physical manufacturing facility is presupposed. If a commercial office or storage site is used, the SARL must obtain a fire safety certification in accordance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 February 1986 on fire safety in buildings; a structural load inspection and an occupancy permit (autorisation d'exploitation) issued by the competent municipal authority; and an occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), 45 boulevard Roosevelt, L-2983 Luxembourg (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu and MyGuichet.lu). VAT and registration duties: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDTVA), 1-3 avenue Guillaume, L-1651 Luxembourg (portal: guichet.lu and MyGuichet.lu). Customs and excise: Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL via a notary and file with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) to obtain the RCS registration number (matricule). Step 2: File VAT registration form (Formulaire 640 'Déclaration de début d'activité') with the AEDTVA to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) required for all taxable supplies. Step 3: Register with the ACD for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; the ACD establishes the national corporate tax file (NIF/reference number). Step 4: Apply for an EORI number with the Customs and Excise Administration before the first export or import transaction. Step 5: Foreign entities without a Luxembourg seat may register directly for VAT via the AEDTVA using the non-established taxable person procedure (Form 640), with no physical establishment required; a Luxembourg tax representative may be mandated in specific cases.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (non-transparent, resident corporation). A Luxembourg SARL is a body corporate taxable on its worldwide income; it is subject to corporate income tax (IRC) at 17% (plus 7% solidarity surcharge, effective 18.19%), municipal business tax (ICC) at the applicable communal rate (6.75%–13.85%; Luxembourg City base 6.75%), and net wealth tax (IF). The SARL is neither a pass-through entity nor eligible for territorial profit exemption absent treaty or statutory regime application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law does not provide US-style check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections include: (i) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election for fully consolidated Luxembourg subsidiaries held directly or indirectly at 95%; (ii) optional VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) for eligible related parties; (iii) participation exemption election (50% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains) subject to holding-period and substance conditions; (iv) option for the partial-inclusion tax regime on qualifying foreign permanent-establishment income; hybrid mismatch adjustments follow mandatory ATAD transposition (LIR articles 168sexies et seq.) with no elective carve-outs. No sub-national tax distinctions apply (unitary national regime).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA), implemented under the amended Luxembourg VAT law of 12 February 1979 in conformity with EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 25,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the domestic small business franchise exemption (Article 57 of the 1979 VAT law). Non-resident suppliers and distance sellers have no right to the exemption and must register from the first euro of Luxembourg supplies; intra-EU distance sales of goods up to EUR 10,000 per calendar year remain taxable in Luxembourg unless the supplier elects destination-state taxation via the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No continuous transaction controls (CTC), fiscal API clearance, or digital stamping regime is in force in Luxembourg as of 2025. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary; B2G e-invoicing is mandatory through the PEPPOL network under EU Directive 2014/55/EU. VAT compliance is discharged via periodic VAT returns (Form 640, filed monthly, quarterly or annually through MyGuichet.lu), recapitulative EC Sales Lists, and Intrastat declarations where applicable; EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) real-time digital reporting for intra-EU supplies is expected to apply from 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to territories outside the EU qualify for the 0% rate under Article 54 of the amended Luxembourg VAT law of 12 February 1979, provided the POD apparel is physically dispatched or transported out of the EU within three months of supply and the supplier retains conclusive documentary evidence. Intra-EU dispatches to a VAT-registered purchaser in another Member State are zero-rated under Article 55 of the same law. B2B print-on-demand services supplied to non-EU customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (subject to reversal where applicable). The invoice must state the applicable zero-rating reference and be matched to the export customs declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/Single Administrative Document) with electronic filing through the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration
Export Accompanying Document (EAD) and exit confirmation from the EU customs office
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) evidencing consignee, destination and date of departure
Commercial invoice, packing list and transport documents (CMR/CTN) supporting the export transaction
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank FX inflow statement evidencing receipt of foreign currency consideration from the overseas buyer
EORI registration number and, for intra-EU supplies, the recapitulative EC Sales List (ESL) filing reference
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating claims (including fictitious exports, false consignee declarations, or non-repatriation of foreign currency proceeds) are subject to combined audits by the ACD, AEDTVA and the Customs and Excise Administration. Retrospective reassessments can claw back the zero-rated treatment, deny input VAT recovery, and impose statutory late-interest. Administrative fines for VAT evasion may reach up to 100% of the evaded tax under Article 59 of the 1979 VAT law, with criminal exposure for intentional fraud including fines and imprisonment. The standard five-year reassessment limitation is extended to ten years in cases of established fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; prudential and conduct supervision of credit institutions and payment/electronic-money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration; exchange-control authority is fully subordinated to the ECB framework and to the Luxembourg law of 27 November 1986 on balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts for residents and non-residents. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Directive 88/361/EEC prohibit any exchange controls on capital movements and payments between Luxembourg and the rest of the world. There is no prior authorization regime, no currency-conversion permit, no repatriation quota, and no restriction on profit remittance, dividend distribution, loan repayment, shareholder return or trade settlement. The only remittance friction is tax-based: dividends paid to an EU parent satisfying the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) conditions (qualifying holding of at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding period) are exempt from Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; distributions to non-EU shareholders are subject to the standard 15% dividend withholding tax under Article 147 LIR, mitigated or eliminated under an applicable double tax treaty. Anti-abuse and transfer-pricing controls (Article 56 LIR, ATAD 1/2, thin-capitalization and interest limitation rules) discipline pricing of intragroup funding but do not restrict exchange convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg law imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into EUR, and no surrender ratio. A Luxembourg SARL may lawfully retain USD, GBP, CNY or any other currency balances onshore or offshore. The sole administrative requirement is statistical: resident credit institutions execute BCL reference reporting (collecte de données de référence) for balance-of-payments purposes, requiring the company to provide the economic nature of each transaction (e.g., 'export proceeds of goods', 'trade payables') for wire transfers typically at or above EUR 12,500 or equivalent; this reporting does not create an authorization, conversion or repatriation obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account (Compte de dépôt de capital)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a supplementary operational settlement and FX rail; Low as the sole primary banking relationship for a Luxembourg SARL. A non-Luxembourg EU/EEA electronic-money institution (EMI) licensed under PSD2 (e.g., Wise Europe authorised by the National Bank of Belgium, Revolut Bank UAB, or an equivalent passporting EMI) may bank the SARL on a cross-border services basis without a CSSF licence. A Luxembourg-domiciled EMI would require CSSF authorization under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services, as amended. Material legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot grant credit, take deposits, or settle directly on central-bank money (TARGET2/T2); (ii) balances are protected only through safeguarding arrangements with a partner credit institution, not by the EUR 100,000 deposit-guarantee scheme; (iii) Luxembourg notaries, statutory auditors and tax administration substance reviews expect a relationship with a Luxembourg-regulated credit institution, particularly for the capital blocking certificate and for audit confirmations; (iv) Stripe and PayPal are payment acquirers/processing PSPs rather than banking substitutes and should be integrated solely as merchant settlement rails into the treasury structure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated. Luxembourg credit institutions apply a de facto in-person identification requirement for non-resident UBOs and directors of newly incorporated SARLs; at least one physical interview at the bank's Luxembourg branch, or a notarized mandate executed before a Luxembourg notary with the mandate-holder appearing in person, is required before account activation. Remote video-identification is legally available under the 2020 Luxembourg law on electronic identification and trust services and accompanying CSSF guidance, but banks in practice restrict fully remote onboarding to EEA residents able to authenticate through an eIDAS-compliant digital identity. For non-EU principals, the accepted alternative is: (i) appointment of a Luxembourg-resident authorised signatory by board resolution; (ii) the signatory appears physically at the bank; (iii) foreign UBOs execute notarized UBO declarations and source-of-wealth forms certified by a local notary or Luxembourg honorary consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated PSP settlement flows: Stripe/PayPal payouts arrive as pooled, anonymous lump sums without customer names, which can be misread as third-party or unusual fund movements inconsistent with the stated POD retail business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant service agreements with Stripe and PayPal; 6 to 12 months of PSP payout statements and settlement reports (gross/net); platform transaction-level exports in CSV with order ID, SKU, customer country and payment reference; PCI-DSS Attestation of Compliance; published refund and chargeback policy; and a written financial-flow diagram showing customer -> acquirer -> PSP -> SARL settlement account mechanics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Geographic supply-chain friction: trade payables to third-country POD producers (e.g., China, Vietnam, United States) from a Luxembourg retail SARL with no physical warehouse or local inventory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed POD production and fulfilment agreements; supplier KYB extracts including business registration and beneficial owner confirmation; sample commercial invoices matching production volumes; HS classification codes (e.g., HS 6109, 6114, 6211) and Incoterms (DAP/DDP); logistics waybills from USPS, DHL, DPD or similar carriers; and a board resolution approving the supplier list and payment terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO layering through non-resident holding structures: ultimate natural persons holding indirectly via a chain of non-EU SPVs, triggering enhanced due diligence and RBE cross-checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association of the SARL; RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing extract identifying all natural persons with more than 25% interest; signed corporate organigram; passport copies of each ultimate natural person; AML source-of-wealth questionnaire; and a bank reference letter from the parent group's existing regulated financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Refund and reversal opacity: frequent e-commerce refunds, chargebacks and PSP adjustments creating circular or reversed flows that may resemble layering or unauthorized payment activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Publicly available refund policy; PSP refund and chargeback dispute logs; reconciliation ledger mapping every refund to the original transaction; VAT/e-commerce return excerpts; and an explanatory note from the statutory auditor confirming that refund liabilities are operating obligations and not client consignments or fiduciary balances.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial subscription of SARL share capital, funds are deposited in a EUR capital-blocking account (compte de dépôt de capital) at a Luxembourg or EEA credit institution; the bank issues a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage de fonds) to the notary; upon signature of the notarial deed, funds are released to the operational account. Subsequent capital increases are routed via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR or SWIFT MT103 for foreign currency using ISO 20022 Purpose Code CAPC ('Capital Payment') or INTC ('Intra-Company Payment') where the contributing shareholder is a group company; the bank requires the shareholders' resolution or notarial deed excerpt for its file. E-commerce operating inflows settle through Stripe/PayPal payouts to the SARL's designated EUR and USD accounts; verification by the receiving bank matches the PSP settlement reference to the registered merchant account ID and the PSP master agreement. For BCL balance-of-payments reference reporting, the resident bank must record a purpose/motif économique for transactions with non-residents at or above EUR 12,500 equivalent; supporting documentation includes the underlying commercial invoice, share capital resolution, or loan agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: (i) EU/EEA POD suppliers and fulfilment partners: SEPA Credit Transfer cleared via TARGET Services (T2) or SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) with EPC purpose code TRAD or SUPP, settlement in EUR within the same business day. (ii) Non-EEA suppliers (US, UK, CN, HK): SWIFT MT103 through the correspondent network in USD, GBP or CNY, accompanied by the commercial invoice and BCL motif économique reference for trade payables. (iii) Bulk or bespoke procurement orders above approximately EUR 50,000 (e.g., regional batch production runs): irrevocable documentary letters of credit governed by UCP 600, issued via SWIFT MT700 against presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list and certificate of origin; for order-by-order POD micro-flows, LCs are economically unsuitable due to issuance and acceptance charges of 0.5 to 1.5 percent per annum plus USD 50 to 150 per amendment, so open-account telegraphic transfer with 30 to 60 day terms is the prevailing market standard. (iv) Ancillary marketing and platform payments (Meta, Google, Shopify apps) use commercial card rails or SEPA Direct Debit (SDD B2B). The SARL should maintain segregated EUR and USD accounts to avoid repeated forced conversion at bank spreads; FX conversion should be executed only on consolidated monthly positions through a dedicated FX-forward line.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX Forward contracts with tenors up to 12 months documented under an ISDA Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex or an FX-specific ACDA governed by Luxembourg or English law, covering USD settlement proceeds retained from US POD sales
EUR/USD FX Swaps (near leg and far leg combination) for rolling management of USD balances across quarterly VAT and payroll windows
FX Spot contracts for immediate conversion of USD, GBP or CNH proceeds into EUR for operational disbursement, executed on consolidated PSP treasury balances to minimize spread costs

CNH/CNY deliverable FX forwards for RMB payables to Chinese POD suppliers via offshore CNH clearing through Luxembourg-licensed credit institutions and their Hong Kong or Mainland correspondent branches

Currency options (EUR call / USD put) permitted under MiFID II professional-client rules where a genuine hedging exposure is evidenced, limited to premium-payment structures and prohibited for naked option-selling without an underlying commercial exposure

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) permissible but not applicable to EUR/USD because EUR/USD is a fully convertible deliverable pair; NDFs are reserved exclusively for residual exposures to non-convertible counterpart currencies (e.g., VND, IDR, KRW) should the supplier base expand into those jurisdictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts (Comptes Annuels) – balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, filed in XBRL format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of financial year-end; filing with the RCS within 8 months of financial year-end (e.g., 31 August for a 31 December year-end SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice (mise en demeure) from LBR; fines of EUR 500–25,000 imposed on directors; persistent non-filing may trigger judicial or administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data filed in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each 12-month anniversary of the entity's RBE registration date; any shareholding transfer must be declared to the RBE within one month of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 under the RBE Law for late, incomplete or inaccurate filing; infringements may be made public

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return covering Corporate Income Tax (IRC), Municipal Business Tax (ICC) and Net Wealth Tax (IF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May following the tax year for calendar-year companies; customary extension for e-filing and certified tax advisors (typically extended to later months of the same year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-interest of 0.6% per month; late-payment surcharge up to 10%; ex-officio assessment by the ACD; minimum net wealth tax of EUR 3,545 per annum remains payable even in loss-making years

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (reviseur d'entreprises agree) is triggered when the SARL exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average headcount of 50. Audit is also compulsory for consolidated group reporting, when shareholders holding at least 25% of capital so request, or under specific supervisory rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU, as amended by the Law of 18 December 2015); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted only for undertakings that are expressly entitled to the option; small undertakings must apply Lux GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must confirm the accuracy of all RBE data annually within one month of the 12-month anniversary of its RBE registration; any share transfer requires RBE disclosure within 30 days and immediate updating of the shareholders' register (registre des parts); the annual confirmation does not replace event-driven filings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Administration Documentation and Service Contracts)
Minute Book (Registre des Proces-Verbaux of General Meetings and Board Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,500–EUR 3,500 (approx. USD 1,650–USD 3,850) per annum for fiduciary, registered-office and corporate domiciliation services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 5,000–EUR 15,000 (approx. USD 5,500–USD 16,500) per annum for a certified statutory audit of a small POD-retail SARL where the audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined: 17% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays. Principal incentives: 80% exemption for net income derived from qualifying IP assets under the Luxembourg IP regime; investment tax credit of 12% on qualifying new tangible fixed assets (up to 18% for small/medium entities); participation exemption of up to 100% for dividends and capital gains from qualifying shareholdings; exemption for profits attributable to a foreign permanent establishment under certain conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the eCDF/RTS portal, authenticated through MyGuichet.lu; required also for municipal business tax and net wealth tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: By 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end unless an extension is granted by the Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes – ACD).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, registered address, Luxembourg Business Register (RCS) number, and taxpayer number (NIF/LUID).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident entities operating through a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE), enter the PE-specific identification number assigned by the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates according to the audited annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE accounting period aligned with the head office fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss per statutory accounts after all accounting provisions, depreciation, and reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record net profit attributable exclusively to the Luxembourg PE; remove head-office general expenses not deductible under the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add back non-deductible expenses (e.g. corporate income tax, VAT penalties, fines, excess interest) and deduct tax-exempt income (e.g. qualifying participation dividends, IP exempt income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back expenses recharged to the PE that exceed arm's-length remuneration; deduct only PE-exempt items applicable under domestic law.
Compute PE taxable income after applying Luxembourg-specific source rules and DTA provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carry-forward tax losses applied from prior fiscal years (unlimited carry-forward under Luxembourg law).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs may only use losses previously incurred within Luxembourg and attributable to the same PE activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable base after loss compensation, subject to corporate income tax and municipal business tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This final amount is the PE taxable base on which the Luxembourg tax liability is computed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of the tax due if the return is not lodged by the statutory deadline; late payment interest accrues at 0.75% per month on overdue amounts; additional administrative fines up to EUR 1,000. Willful non-filing or false filing can trigger criminal penalty and imprisonment of responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower or zero dividend withholding rate under a Double Tax Agreement or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the beneficial owner must submit a Form 100 (or the ACD current waiver/refund form) to the Luxembourg ACD, attaching a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's state of residence and evidence of holding period (≥10% shareholding for ≥12 months under EU directive). The relief is applied at source or via a refund process; processing normally takes 8–12 weeks.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rate is 0% for royalties and interest paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-residents; treaty rates are generally 0% or reduced, with no Luxembourg domestic withholding on such cross-border outgoing payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold expressly prescribed for Local File or Master File in Luxembourg domestic law; however, EU Country-by-Country reporting applies to ultimate parent groups with consolidated annual revenue ≥ EUR 750 million. All taxpayers must maintain transfer pricing documentation sufficient to support related-party transactions upon ACD request; documentation should be available before filing for fiscal-year 2024.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain type-based Economic Substance Regulations akin to offshore jurisdictions, but the OECD substance requirement and the EU General Anti-Tax Avoidance Rule (ATAD GAAR) apply. For a Print-on-Demand retail entity, sufficient commercial substance includes real staff in Luxembourg, substantive management decisions, actual e-commerce contracts, and a meaningful operational presence. Failure to demonstrate substance allows the ACD to recharacterize income, deny treaty benefits, and treat the SARL as a transparent shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Failure to Declare Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally under-declaring online sales proceeds received through Stripe or PayPal, omitting chargebacks, misclassing personal expenditure as business expenses, or destroying transactional records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of responsible persons up to 5 years under Luxembourg Criminal Tax Law; reassessment of evaded income plus late payment interest at 0.75% per month; administrative penalty of 100% of the evaded tax for bad faith.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to personal criminal imprisonment and travel bans; civil liability of officers for restitution of corporate tax debts and fines; piercing the corporate veil is permissible where the SARL is a mere alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL with no real staff, no physical office, and stripping profits through artificial service fees to a zero-tax related party; using a mailbox director or sham shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits and domestic participation exemption; profit recharacterization to the controlling shareholder; levy of 15% dividend withholding tax on redistributed sums plus penalty of 25% of the additional tax under GAAR legislation; forced deregistration by the Luxembourg Business Registers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners risk asset freeze orders, disqualification from any directorship for up to 10 years, and joint and several liability for the company's tax and penalty amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) details in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) or failing to maintain up-to-date UBO documentation in the anti-money laundering file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines ranging from EUR 100 to EUR 5,000 per violation; additional daily enforcement penalties of EUR 250 per day for non-compliance; criminal fines for deliberate false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is personally liable for fines; directors may receive criminal record entry and be temporarily barred from conducting commercial activities in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length margins with related parties, inflating commission payments to low-tax distributors, or allocating e-commerce platform intellectual property to a zero-tax jurisdiction without demonstrated economic substance or benchmarking analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment to realign profits; additional tax assessments plus monthly interest; penalty up to 100% of the additional assessed tax for deliberate mispricing; potential referral to the Mutual Agreement Procedure or EU arbitration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing false contemporaneous documentation can face criminal prosecution for aiding tax fraud; they may be held personally liable for the penalty component and subject to a European Arrest Warrant in cross-border investigations.
